newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Tender details for Ecuador Emetel ready next week.
newsitem.headline: Tender details for Ecuador Emetel ready next week.

text.p: Tender specifications for the sale of 35 percent of Ecuador's state telecommunications company Emetel will be ready for sale next week, a government official said Thursday.
Leonardo Escobar, executive director of the National Council of Modernization (CONAM), told reporters the specifications will cost $30,000 each.
"Next week CONAM will call for international bids for the specifications. Five international operators will be participating," he added.
U.S. firms MCI Communications Corp and GTE Corp, Italy's STET Spa, Telefonica de Espana and Korea Telecom said in November they wanted to take part.

Ecuador's government is hoping to raise $1.0 billion through the sale of a 35 percent stake in Emetel, which has assets worth $4.0 billion, according to official estimates. Before the 35 percent stake is sold, Emetel will be split in two by the government.
One of the requirements that will be imposed on the winner of the stake will be to complete 2.5 million local telephone lines compared with the current 800,000.
